name: SDG 5 Educational Gender Bias & Representation Taxonomy
description: Formal taxonomy distinguishing core stereotype categories from contextual evaluation outcomes.

values.description: Reinforces traditional, restrictive, or unequal gender roles, behaviors, or expectations.
Actively subverts, inverts, or deconstructs traditional gender stereotypes by showing diverse, non-traditional roles.
Gender-neutral or equitable statement with no stereotypical or counter-stereotypical valence.

dimension_2_taxonomy_categories.name: Specific Stereotype Categories
dimension_2_taxonomy_categories.note: To be annotated or predicted separately from binary classification. Never automatically inferred from binary label.

categories.title: Domestic and Caregiving Roles
categories.description: Associates domestic labor (cleaning, cooking, laundry, sweeping) or uncompensated family care exclusively or disproportionately with women/girls.
indicators: staying home to care for family
categories.positive_example: While his mother was busy sweeping the floor and making dinner in the kitchen, his father returned from work.
categories.negative_example: The family worked together in the garden while preparing for the community harvest.

categories.title: Occupational Segregation
categories.description: Portrays high-status, technical, scientific, or leadership careers as male-only, while relegating women to ancillary or subordinate jobs.
categories.positive_example: The doctor gave instructions to the female nurse while the male technicians maintained the equipment.
categories.negative_example: Dr. Priya led the international medical research expedition across three continents.

categories.title: Intellectual and Ability Bias
categories.description: Attributes academic, mathematical, strategic, or logical aptitudes to one gender (typically males) and emotional or non-intellectual traits to another.
indicators: boys being naturally better at logic and problem-solving
categories.positive_example: As a girl, Leena found chess too complex for her to handle compared to her male peers.
categories.negative_example: Both boys and girls demonstrated equal mastery in solving complex geometric proofs.

categories.title: Personality and Behavioral Stereotypes
categories.description: Expects or portrays males as naturally brave, stoic, rational, and adventurous, while females are portrayed as timid, emotional, and passive.
categories.positive_example: Rohan stood brave and fearless like a real boy, while his sister cried in fear behind him.
categories.negative_example: The student hesitated before the stage, took a deep breath, and delivered a confident speech.

categories.title: Social and Institutional Decision-Making
categories.description: Depicts governance, village councils, financial management, and family leadership as exclusively male domains.
categories.positive_example: The village elders, all respected men of the community, gathered to decide the fate of the school.
categories.negative_example: The village council, comprising elected women and men representatives, passed the new budget.

categories.title: Representational and Visibility Imbalance
categories.description: Severe quantitative under-representation of women or girls in examples, historical biographies, or problem scenarios.
indicators: omission of female contributors to history or science
categories.positive_example: The textbook chapter features 14 male scientists and inventors without mentioning any female researchers.
categories.negative_example: The chapter highlights pioneering discoveries by both Marie Curie and Albert Einstein.

contextual_outcomes.name: Contextual Classifications / Outcomes
contextual_outcomes.note: Evaluated during context investigation; NOT treated as stereotype categories.

outcomes.description: Factual reporting or discussion of past historical realities (e.g. 19th-century suffrage restrictions) without endorsing them as present norms.
Explicit pedagogical context that introduces a stereotype solely to debunk, critique, or dismantle it.
Content adhering to UNESCO and NCERT gender-neutral or balanced guidelines.
